At the breakwater

We reached the outer wall just as the ferry entered the bay. Its wake folded into the small waves that ran along the harbour steps.

We walked past the moorings to the last stone on the wall. The light on the tower was pale in the clear morning air.

Field log

Clouds gathered behind the headland by midday. The wind was still light enough for the flags to hang against the signal mast.

When the boat returned, the tide covered the lowest step. The bell rang once as the crew brought the first rope ashore.
